fatal_errors: The hypothesis proposes generic FCC metals, whereas the target materials are single-BCC-phase NbMoTaW and NbMoTaWRe refractory high-entropy-alloy films.
It fails to identify Re-containing NbMoTaWRe as the material with improved post-irradiation ductility and embrittlement resistance.
It replaces the target intervention—Re addition and 120 keV He2+ implantation—with in-situ tensile microscopy.
The proposed dislocation-glide, twinning, and grain-boundary-sliding mechanism omits the target defect-sink, vacancy-annihilation, He-bubble suppression, and grain-boundary-embrittlement mechanism.
No supporting evidence is cited, and the proposed baseline and applicability boundary are undefined relative to the target system.
explanation: The response is a generic statement about FCC-metal ductility rather than a reconstruction of the reported BCC refractory-alloy study. Its only condition-level overlap is room-temperature mechanical testing. It misses the NbMoTaW versus NbMoTaWRe comparison, helium-irradiation conditions, Re-induced grain refinement and amorphous boundary regions, suppression of grain-boundary He bubbles, and the observed reduction in irradiation hardening and embrittlement. The suggested experiment could test broad microstructure–ductility correlations, but it does not discriminate the target Re/He-damage mechanism.
